topics.flagship-ru-ua: A Ukrainian drone attack damaged a Russian Yandex data centre east of Moscow, disrupting operations at the technology and AI facility. Germany's foreign minister rejected Trump's demands and reaffirmed full support for Zelenskyy, stating Berlin will continue pressuring Russia to end the war. Additional reporting indicates Russian strikes on Ukrainian data centers and civilian infrastructure, with three children among 11 killed in airstrikes on Zaporizhzhia residential buildings.
topics.flagship-ir-il: Saudi coalition blamed the Houthi group for a major missile strike on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh that killed 12 people and wounded over 300, prompting flight suspensions and a mass medical emergency response. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio called for an immediate end to the attacks and confirmed an American citizen was among the dead. Multiple sources report the incident as part of an expanding pattern of Houthi attacks against Saudi Arabian targets.
topics.T15: Panama declared a state of emergency as powerful earthquake aftershocks rattled communities, though officials reported no deaths. Tornadoes in Sicily destroyed a school and injured dozens, with over 270 pupils inside at the time of impact.
topics.T01: Fighting is intensifying between Yemeni government forces and the Houthi rebel group as part of wider regional conflict. A US diplomat argued markets are overestimating the threat of war over Taiwan, claiming Beijing does not seek conflict.
topics.T02: A drone strike blamed on Sudan's paramilitaries killed 41 displaced people near the Ethiopian border. Multiple humanitarian crises are developing, including child marriage in Gaza as schools remain closed and families face displacement and poverty.
topics.T04: Marshall Billingslea revealed that a Soviet defector exposed a massive Russian biological weapons program involving antibiotic-resistant plague research, reviving concerns over Russia's bioweapons capabilities. Commentary warns of additional health threats in melting Russian permafrost, and Washington confirmed its first H5N1 bird flu cases in dairy cattle in Yakima County.
topics.T05: Pakistan's prime minister imposed emergency rule in a province governed by Imran Khan's party, citing the provincial government's alleged disengagement from counterterrorism efforts. Germany's intelligence reputation faces damage following an investigation into an arrested spy chief with alleged Chinese connections.
topics.T06: France student protests over crumbling schools have cost at least 30 million euros and resulted in nearly 7,000 arrests, with reports indicating left-wing extremist elements have infiltrated the demonstrations. India's police detained founders and dozens of protesters from the 'Cockroach' movement ahead of a major protest calling for the chief election commissioner's resignation.
topics.T07: Japan faces a contentious debate over potential modifications to its three non-nuclear principles.
topics.T08: An Israeli mother who lost her son in the October 7 Hamas massacre nearly lost her daughter when a flydubai flight was subject to a hijacking attempt. Young men in Myanmar live in fear of being forcibly recruited into the junta's army amid an ongoing war of attrition against ethnic militias.
topics.T10: Taiwan announced plans to boost military defense spending to deter war with China, following US President Trump's request that Taiwan pay for US protection. The UK MOD and QinetiQ launched Project Safari to provide SMEs expanded access to test and evaluation facilities.
topics.T11: Indonesian and Australian armies conducted joint combat training in the 'Wirra Jaya Ausindo 2026' military exercise in Semarang, Central Java.
topics.T13: At least 109 migrants, including 15 children, died and approximately 116 went missing when a boat sank off Djibouti's shores in early Friday morning, according to a UN agency. Italy's 'Schools Decree' capping foreign-born pupils at 30% has sparked wider European debate over integration policies.
